title: How to Connect GPT-6 Astra to DaVinci Resolve With MCP
description:
Follow me and DM me "DA VINCI" on IG/FB only 👇

GPT-6 Astra edited this video inside DaVinci Resolve through the new DaVinci Resolve MCP.

I gave it photos and asked it to make a video. The bridge connected ChatGPT to the editor, so Astra worked inside DaVinci Resolve instead of sending me editing instructions.

Here’s the full setup:

1. Download DaVinci Resolve 21.0.3.

2. Open Codex, choose GPT-6 Astra, and set the reasoning effort to light.

3. Give Astra the DaVinci Resolve MCP repository link. Let it handle the setup.

4. Restart DaVinci Resolve after the installation finishes.

5. Create a new project. Open Workspace, choose Scripts, then run resolve_bridge.

6. Point Astra to your photos and ask it to make a video.

The order matters. Finish the MCP setup before restarting DaVinci Resolve. Then create the project and launch resolve_bridge from the Scripts menu. Once the connection is live, give Astra your source photos and a clear editing request.

This workflow turns a chat request into work inside a desktop video editor. You still choose the photos and describe the video you want. Astra handles the editing task through the MCP bridge.

GPT-6 Astra just dropped. And OpenAI says it can do complex research tasks that would take a human several days. But what if the biggest change in AI isn’t that it can answer harder questions? What if it’s that you can give it a problem, walk away, and come back to find the work done?
Because that’s what makes Astra interesting. For the first time, we’re seeing AI move beyond the chatbot. It can open software, work with files, navigate websites, analyse information, and complete tasks across your computer. And when you combine that with AI agents that can coordinate with each other, you start getting something that looks less like an assistant and more like an entire digital workforce.
But here’s the question nobody can really answer yet. If AI can increasingly do the work, what happens to the people whose jobs are built around thinking, researching, creating, and making decisions? And is this what the beginning of AGI actually looks like? Today, we’re going to find out how far Astra has come, how close it is to becoming a coworker, and what that means for the future of knowledge work.

title: Why The Prompt Matters Less Than The Context
description:
Join the AI Evals October 2026 cohort: https://maven.com/parlance-labs/evals?promoCode=yt-2026

If you're new to my channel, my name is Hamel Husain. I spent 20 years in data and machine learning at banks, startups, Airbnb, GitHub, before most people knew what any of that meant. In 2023 I started advising AI companies and noticed the same gap everywhere: nobody had a real way to test, measure, and improve their AI products. They were shipping on vibes.

So I started documenting how to fix that. What I built became the most popular evals course in the world: 4,500+ engineers and PMs from OpenAI, Google, Meta, Anthropic, and more. My colleague Shreya Shankar and I are also co-authoring the O'Reilly book on it.

This channel is where I share what I actually know about building AI products that hold up.

How I got here...
2003: Built credit-risk models right out of college (Math and Industrial Engineering). SQL, scripting, data visualization. The foundational stuff.
2005: Data consulting across a dozen industries. Reading messy data and finding where processes were broken. Same muscle I use now for error analysis on LLM products.
2008: Burned out and went to law school. Learned two things: I can write, and I'm an engineer who was kidding himself.
2010: Back to consulting. Predictive models across demand forecasting, marketing, and customer service.
2014: Joined DataRobot to sit near Kaggle grandmasters. Thousands of reps building predictive models fast.
2016: Data Scientist at Airbnb. Inherited a badly overfit growth model that had been running in prod. Helped set up systems so it couldn't happen again.
2017: Machine learning at GitHub. Led the team that built CodeSearchNet, a benchmark for semantic code search. Underneath, it was a set of evals for code understanding. OpenAI later used it to evaluate their first code embeddings, which became groundwork for the earliest coding models.
2022: Left to turn an open source developer tool into a company. ChatGPT shipped and the bet stopped making sense. I walked away.
2023: Independent consultant. Advised 50+ companies, startups to Fortune 500s. Everyone had the same gap: no real way to test or improve AI beyond vibe checks. I started documenting the fix.

This channel is the unfiltered version of what I've learned. What works, what doesn't, and how to build AI that actually holds up.

Hamel
